name: hearing loss overview
title: Hearing loss: the Weber and Rinne together split conductive (ear canal; otitis media; a fixed or broken middle ear) from sensorineural (sudden, an emergency; gradual and symmetric; one-sided and progressive, a vestibular schwannoma until proven otherwise; other causes: congenital, a transverse temporal bone fracture and more); a tier under each group traces the sound path it affects; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment, and otitis media lists its complications

root.title: Hearing loss: is sound BLOCKED before the cochlea, or is the cochlea or nerve DAMAGED?
lines: ask: loudness or clarity · duration · sudden or insidious · rate · one or both ears · pain (the T's), discharge, fullness, tinnitus, vertigo, facial or trigeminal symptoms
512 Hz tuning forks, ALWAYS both: Weber pushed hard on the midline (forehead, nose, tooth; detects 5 dB) + Rinne (mastoid, then beside the ear; normal air > bone)
e.g. Weber → RIGHT = right conductive OR left sensorineural · Rinne decides: right bone > air → RIGHT conductive

audiogram: dB is logarithmic (+10 dB = 10× intensity, ~2× loudness) · conversation 60 · lawnmower 90 · rock concert 120 · gunshot 140 · newborns: auditory brainstem response · CT: bone, ossicles · MRI: cerebellopontine angle
a SUDDEN conductive loss can wait; a SUDDEN sensorineural loss is an EMERGENCY

groups.title: CONDUCTIVE
lines: Weber → the AFFECTED ear · Rinne there: bone > air
audiogram: bone normal, air down (an air-bone gap)

groups.title: SENSORINEURAL
lines: Weber → the NORMAL ear · Rinne: air > bone
audiogram: bone down, air the same as bone
damage to cochlea or nerve cannot be repaired

tiers.title: Sound path: canal → drum → ossicles
lines: • ossicles: air pressure → force on the oval window → moves fluid

tiers.title: Cochlea → nerve → cortex
lines: • oval window → scala vestibuli → helicotrema → scala tympani → round window
• TONOTOPIC: stiff base = HIGH pitch · floppy apex = low
• inner hair cells transduce, outer amplify
• spiral ganglion → CN VIII → brainstem → medial geniculate → superior temporal gyrus

head: h
Ear canal
wax · foreign body · exostoses · otitis externa
pres: • bacterial: itchy, painful, swollen, sore on pulling the pinna
• fungal: severe itch, less pain, after antibiotics
inv: • bacterial: Pseudomonas, then Staph aureus, E. coli
tx: • fungal: fluconazole or clotrimazole (intact drum: Locacorten-Vioform)
dermatitis (local steroid), Q-tips, fibrosis traps wax · may need excision + graft

head: h
Otitis media
the commonest middle ear cause
peak 6-11 months · 2/3 by age 1 · 1/2 have > 3 by age 3
pres: pain, fever, irritability · bulging drum · discharge
• Strep pneumoniae 30-40% · H. influenzae 20-30% · Moraxella 10-15% · group A strep 2-4%
inv: Fluid in BOTH ears for 3 months
tx: or watch 48-72 h in lower-risk children · treat pain
• effusion both ears > 3 months + > 20 dB loss in the better ear
• intermittent fluid with a hearing aid · chronic drum atrophy

head: h
Drum or ossicles
perforation · otosclerosis · longitudinal fracture
also cholesteatoma, adhesive otitis media
pres: • otosclerosis: NORMAL drum, no trauma or infection · bone fixes the STAPES footplate
• longitudinal fracture (80%, side blow): unconscious, bleeding from or behind the drum, hearing loss · canal tear, ossicles disrupted
inv: otosclerosis: conductive or mixed, rising curve, Carhart's notch
tx: • perforation: keep dry, 80% heal; else tympanoplasty
• aids: air (behind or in the ear), or bone-conduction (BAHA, Bonebridge)

head: h
SUDDEN sensorineural
onset < 3 days · EMERGENCY
tx: Steroids by mouth or into the ear

head: h
Gradual, symmetric
presbycusis · noise · ototoxic drugs
pres: • presbycusis: commonest, HIGH pitches first (basal hair cells), 30% over 65, 50% over 75, men more
• noise > 85 dB (max for an 8-hour shift): work, recreation, guns (asymmetric)
• aminoglycosides, cisplatin, carboplatin, vincristine, loop diuretics
~ASA and quinine: reversible · macrolides: temporary · gentamicin used on purpose
tx: cochlear implant: bypasses hair cells, stimulates CN VIII (needs a working nerve)

head: h
ONE-sided, progressive
vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma)
pres: ~commonest cerebellopontine angle mass · both sides = NF2

head: h
Other sensorineural
congenital · trauma · systemic
pres: • through the otic capsule, rarely recovers
